assumptions.choice: Stop level is computed from the order's actual fill price (backtrader's position.price, captured in notify_order) rather than the signal bar's close, since backtrader fills entry orders at the next bar's open.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'stop-loss 2% away from entry price'; the true entry price is the filled price, not the close on the signal bar.

assumptions.choice: Manual stop logic checked once per bar by comparing the bar's close price to the fixed 2% stop level.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly allows 'Backtrader stop orders or manual stop logic'; manual close-based checking is simplest to reconcile with the other exit conditions (RSI reversal, time exit) without managing multiple concurrent order types.

assumptions.choice: A new qualifying entry is allowed later the same day after a position is closed (stop/RSI/time), as long as it is still within the 11:30-14:30 window and daily bias is unchanged.
assumptions.reason: The spec's 'at most one position at a time' is a concurrency constraint, not an explicit once-per-day limit; nothing in the spec restricts trade count per day.

assumptions.choice: The 11:30 bar itself is eligible for entries (window treated as inclusive of 11:30), since that bar's close is simultaneously used to determine the morning bias.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the midday window as '11:30-14:30' and derives the bias from the 11:30 close, implying trading can begin on that same bar.

assumptions.choice: Relied on backtrader's automatic minperiod (max of RSI(14) and 20-bar volume SMA); next() is not called until bar 20, so the first trading day may have no signals.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default: no manual bar-skipping beyond backtrader's automatic minperiod.

assumptions.choice: Assumed the PandasData feed's datetime values represent US/Eastern wall-clock time directly, and compared bar times against naive datetime.time objects (09:30, 11:30, 14:30) accordingly.
assumptions.reason: The data description states bars are already timestamped in US/Eastern (-04:00); backtrader operates on the local wall-clock component of the feed's datetimes.
